name: Ezra
charge: Preparing his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments
summary: A ready scribe in the law of Moses came up from Babylon with the king's letter and the king's silver, refused a guard because he had told the king the hand of God is on all that seek him, fasted at the river Ahava, and arrived. He read the law to the people from morning to midday, and they wept, and kept the feast of tabernacles as it had not been kept since Joshua.
offense: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel (Ezra 7:10). The charge of teaching began with the ordering of his own heart and conduct. Royal favor supplied authority and provisions, but his commission remained governed by God's law. At Ahava he gathered the travelers, obtained ministers for the sanctuary, and proclaimed a fast to seek a right way for the people, their little ones, and their substance. Having testified that God's hand was upon those who sought Him, he was ashamed to request soldiers for protection. He also weighed the treasure into appointed hands and required it to be watched and weighed again at Jerusalem (Ezra 8:21-34). Trust in God was joined to careful stewardship.
judgment: And the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the Lord his God upon him. Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, which hath put such a thing as this in the king's heart, to beautify the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem. The hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy, and of such as lay in wait by the way. And all the people went their way to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great mirth, because they had understood the words that were declared unto them. Since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so. And there was very great gladness.
offenseFull: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel (Ezra 7:10). The charge of teaching began with the ordering of his own heart and conduct. Royal favor supplied authority and provisions, but his commission remained governed by God's law.

At Ahava he gathered the travelers, obtained ministers for the sanctuary, and proclaimed a fast to seek a right way for the people, their little ones, and their substance. Having testified that God's hand was upon those who sought Him, he was ashamed to request soldiers for protection. He also weighed the treasure into appointed hands and required it to be watched and weighed again at Jerusalem (Ezra 8:21-34). Trust in God was joined to careful stewardship.
judgmentFull: The Lord delivered the company from enemies along the way. The treasure arrived and was counted and weighed in the house of God. The good hand acknowledged before the journey was acknowledged after it.

At the water gate, Ezra read the law while the Levites gave the sense so the congregation understood. The people wept, received instruction to rejoice and share with those lacking provision, and kept the feast in booths (Nehemiah 8:1-18). The fruit of teaching was understanding followed by obedience, not merely the public reading of words.

entries.commentary: Ezra's genealogy is traced back through Zadok and Phinehas to Eleazar the son of Aaron the chief priest, marking him a priest of the true line. Ezra went up from Babylon a ready scribe in the law of Moses, and the king granted all his requests because the hand of the Most High was upon him.

Some of the children of Israel, priests, Levites, singers, porters, and Nethinims went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes, and Ezra came in the fifth month by the good hand of his God. Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the Most High, to do it, and to teach statutes and judgments in Israel. Preparing the heart means setting the mind and spirit in order, examining oneself, and putting away the weak nature of sin before teaching others. -

Artaxerxes' letter names Ezra a scribe of the law of the God of heaven and grants that any of Israel who willingly desire may go up to Jerusalem with him. The king and his counselors freely offered silver and gold for the house of God, for sacrifices, and for whatever else was needful, drawn even from the king's treasure house. This was favor, letting the captivity return with the treasures of Babylon, as the nations will one day bring back all Israel's substance. -

Artaxerxes decreed to the treasurers beyond the river to supply Ezra speedily with silver, wheat, wine, oil, and salt, so that no wrath would come against the king and his sons. The priests, Levites, singers, porters, and Nethinims were freed from toll, tribute, and custom. This is using the favor of those set over you without abusing it, being granted the freedom the world around still had to pay.

Ezra was told, after the wisdom of his God in his hand, to set magistrates and judges to judge the people and to teach those who did not know the laws of the Most High. The king decreed judgment on any who would not do the law of God and the law of the king. Ezra then blessed the Most High who put it in the king's heart to beautify the house, and was strengthened as the hand of his God was upon him. A heathen king supported the work of the prophets even though he was not an Israelite.

The chief of the fathers and their genealogy are recorded, listing the heads of families who went up with Ezra from Babylon and the number of males with each. Every name is set down deliberately. These were actual people who put their work into the building of the house, and names mean something, which is why Israel desires their names written in the book.

Ezra gathered the company at the river Ahava, abode three days, and viewing the people found none of the sons of Levi, so he sent men of understanding to Iddo at Casiphia to bring ministers for the house. By the good hand of the Most High they brought back men of understanding of the sons of Levi and a large number of Nethinims appointed for the service, all expressed by name. Ezra knew which men among him had understanding and called on them.

Ezra proclaimed a fast at the river Ahava that they might afflict their souls before the Most High and seek of him a right way for themselves, their little ones, and their substance. To afflict the soul is to fast, taking neither food nor water, and one may fast and pray for wisdom and a right path. Ezra was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help against the enemy in the way, having testified that the hand of God is upon all who seek him for good. -

All the people gather as one man into the street before the water gate and ask Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses. He reads before the congregation of men, women, and all that could understand, from morning until midday. The Most High does not favor camps and closed rooms. Ezra stood in the open street to teach, men and women together, and the people were attentive to the words of the law.

Ezra stands upon a pulpit of wood with brothers on his right hand and brothers on his left hand, and opens the book in the sight of all the people, blessing the Most High, to whom the people answer, Amen, Amen. The Levites cause the people to understand the law, reading distinctly and giving the sense so the people understood the reading. Teaching is meant to bring understanding, not merely to be recited.

Nehemiah, Ezra, and the Levites tell the people the day is holy and they should not mourn or weep, for the people wept when they heard the words of the law. They are told to eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared, for the joy of the Most High is their strength. The people go their way to make great mirth because they understood the words that were declared.

On the second day the chief of the fathers, the priests, and the Levites gather to Ezra to understand the words of the law, and they find written that Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month. -

After these things, when Artaxerxes the king of the Persians reigned, came Esdras, of the line of Aaron the chief priest. This Esdras went up from Babylon, as a scribe, being very ready in the law of Moses, that was given by the God of Israel. The king did honour him: for he found grace in his sight in all his requests. Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of the Lord, but taught all Israel the ordinances and judgments.

The commission written from Artaxerxes gave order that such of the nation of the Jews, and of the priests and Levites, as were willing should go with Esdras unto Jerusalem. They were to look unto the affairs of Judea and Jerusalem, agreeably to that which is in the law of the Lord, and to carry the gifts unto the Lord of Israel to Jerusalem. Whatsoever Esdras the priest and reader of the law of the most high God should send for, the keepers of the treasuries in Syria and Phenice should give it him with speed. Let all things be performed after the law of God diligently unto the most high God, that wrath come not upon the kingdom of the king and his sons. No tax nor any other imposition was to be required of the priests, Levites, holy singers, porters, ministers of the temple, or any that have doings in this temple. Thou, Esdras, according to the wisdom of God, ordain judges and justices, that they may judge in all Syria and Phenice: all those that know the law of thy God thou shalt teach, and those that know it not.

Blessed be the only Lord God of my fathers, who hath put these things into the heart of the king, to glorify his house that is in Jerusalem. Therefore was I encouraged by the help of the Lord my God, and gathered together men of Israel to go up with me.

These are the chief, according to their families and several dignities, that went up with Esdras from Babylon in the reign of king Artaxerxes, counted family by family with the number of men. They gathered together at the river called Theras, where they pitched their tents three days, and Esdras surveyed them. When he found there none of the priests and Levites, he sent unto the principal men and learned, that they should send such men as might execute the priest's office in the house of the Lord. By the mighty hand of the Lord they brought unto them skilful men of the sons of Moli the son of Levi, the son of Israel, and of the ministers of the temple whom David had ordained.

There Esdras vowed a fast unto the young men before the Lord, to desire of him a prosperous journey both for them and their children and their cattle. I was ashamed to ask the king footmen and horsemen and conduct for safeguard against our adversaries; for we had said unto the king, that the power of the Lord our God should be with them that seek him, to support them in all ways. Then I separated twelve of the chief of the priests, and weighed them the gold, and the silver, and the holy vessels of the house of our Lord, which the king and his council and the princes and all Israel had given. Ye are holy unto the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the gold and the silver is a vow unto the Lord of our fathers: watch ye, and keep them till ye deliver them to the chief of the priests and Levites at Jerusalem.

From the river Theras we departed the twelfth day of the first month, and came to Jerusalem by the mighty hand of our Lord, which was with us. From the beginning of our journey the Lord delivered us from every enemy, and so we came to Jerusalem. When we had been there three days, the gold and silver that was weighed was delivered in the house of our Lord on the fourth day, all by number and weight, and the whole weight of them was written up the same hour. They that were come out of the captivity offered sacrifice unto the Lord God of Israel, even twelve bullocks for all Israel, fourscore and sixteen rams, threescore and twelve lambs, and twelve goats for a peace offering.

The rulers came unto Esdras and said, The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles. For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity. As soon as I had heard these things, I rent my clothes and the holy garment, and pulled off the hair from off my head and beard, and sat me down sad and very heavy. Rising up from the fast with my clothes and the holy garment rent, and bowing my knees, and stretching forth my hands unto the Lord, I said, O Lord, I am confounded and ashamed before thy face. For our sins are multiplied above our heads, and our ignorances have reached up unto heaven, for ever since the time of our fathers we have been and are in great sin, even unto this day.

In some measure hath mercy been shewed unto us from thee, O Lord, that there should be left us a root and a name in the place of thy sanctuary, and to give us food in the time of our servitude. When we were in bondage we were not forsaken of our Lord, but he made us gracious before the kings of Persia, so that they gave us food, and honoured the temple of our Lord, and raised up the desolate Sion. We have transgressed thy commandments, which thou gavest by the hand of thy servants the prophets, saying, The land which ye enter into to possess as an heritage is a land polluted with the pollutions of the strangers of the land. Therefore now shall ye not join your daughters unto their sons, neither shall ye take their daughters unto your sons; and ye shall never seek to have peace with them, that ye may be strong, and eat the good things of the land, and leave the inheritance of the land unto your children for evermore. All that is befallen is done unto us for our wicked works and great sins; but thou, O Lord, didst make our sins light, and didst give unto us such a root: yet we have turned back again to transgress thy law, and to mingle ourselves with the uncleanness of the nations of the land.

As Esdras in his prayer made his confession, weeping, and lying flat upon the ground before the temple, there gathered unto him from Jerusalem a very great multitude of men and women and children, and there was great weeping among the multitude. Then Jechonias the son of Jeelus, one of the sons of Israel, called out and said, O Esdras, we have sinned against the Lord God, we have married strange women of the nations of the land. Let us make an oath to the Lord, that we will put away all our wives, which we have taken of the heathen, with their children, like as thou hast decreed, and as many as do obey the law of the Lord. Arise, and put in execution: for to thee doth this matter appertain, and we will be with thee: do valiantly. verses.text: This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the Lord God of Israel had given: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the Lord his God upon him.
And there went up some of the children of Israel, and of the priests, and the Levites, and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinims, unto Jerusalem, in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.
For upon the first day of the first month began he to go up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month came he to Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him.
For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.
Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, which hath put such a thing as this in the king’s heart, to beautify the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem:

And hath extended mercy unto me before the king, and his counsellors, and before all the king’s mighty princes. And I was strengthened as the hand of the Lord my God was upon me, and I gathered together out of Israel chief men to go up with me.
Then I proclaimed a fast there, at the river of Ahava, that we might afflict ourselves before our God, to seek of him a right way for us, and for our little ones, and for all our substance.

For I was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy in the way: because we had spoken unto the king, saying, The hand of our God is upon all them for good that seek him; but his power and his wrath is against all them that forsake him.
So we fasted and besought our God for this: and he was intreated of us.

Then we departed from the river of Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, to go unto Jerusalem: and the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy, and of such as lay in wait by the way.
And we came to Jerusalem, and abode there three days.

And all the people gathered themselves together as one man into the street that was before the water gate; and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded to Israel.
And Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation both of men and women, and all that could hear with understanding, upon the first day of the seventh month.

And he read therein before the street that was before the water gate from the morning until midday, before the men and the women, and those that could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law.

And Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, and Shema, and Anaiah, and Urijah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, and Mishael, and Malchiah, and Hashum, and Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people; (for he was above all the people;) and when he opened it, all the people stood up:
And Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God. And all the people answered, Amen, Amen, with lifting up their hands: and they bowed their heads, and worshipped the Lord with their faces to the ground.

Also Jeshua, and Bani, and Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodijah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law: and the people stood in their place.
So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.

And Nehemiah, which is the Tirshatha, and Ezra the priest the scribe, and the Levites that taught the people, said unto all the people, This day is holy unto the Lord your God; mourn not, nor weep. For all the people wept, when they heard the words of the law.

Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
So the Levites stilled all the people, saying, Hold your peace, for the day is holy; neither be ye grieved.
And all the people went their way to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great mirth, because they had understood the words that were declared unto them.
And on the second day were gathered together the chief of the fathers of all the people, the priests, and the Levites, unto Ezra the scribe, even to understand the words of the law.
And they found written in the law which the Lord had commanded by Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month:

And that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities, and in Jerusalem, saying, Go forth unto the mount, and fetch olive branches, and pine branches, and myrtle branches, and palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make booths, as it is written.

So the people went forth, and brought them, and made themselves booths, every one upon the roof of his house, and in their courts, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the street of the water gate, and in the street of the gate of Ephraim.

And all the congregation of them that were come again out of the captivity made booths, and sat under the booths: for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so. And there was very great gladness.

Also day by day, from the first day unto the last day, he read in the book of the law of God. And they kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day was a solemn assembly, according unto the manner.
And after these things, when Artexerxes the king of the Persians reigned came Esdras the son of Saraias, the son of Ezerias, the son of Helchiah, the son of Salum,

The son of Sadduc, the son of Achitob, the son of Amarias, the son of Ezias, the son of Meremoth, the son of Zaraias, the son of Savias, the son of Boccas, the son of Abisum, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest.
This Esdras went up from Babylon, as a scribe, being very ready in the law of Moses, that was given by the God of Israel.
And the king did him honour: for he found grace in his sight in all his requests.
There went up with him also certain of the children of Israel, of the priest of the Levites, of the holy singers, porters, and ministers of the temple, unto Jerusalem,

In the seventh year of the reign of Artexerxes, in the fifth month, this was the king’s seventh year; for they went from Babylon in the first day of the first month, and came to Jerusalem, according to the prosperous journey which the Lord gave them.
For Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of the Lord, but taught all Israel the ordinances and judgments.

For Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of the Lord, but taught all Israel the ordinances and judgments.
